drivingQuestion: Does 'I am avowed from you' alone constitute a vow-intimation?
outcomeNote: Shmuel's qualification stands unchallenged within this unit

segments.he: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ מוּדָּר אֲנִי וְכוּ׳. אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּכוּלָּן עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר, ״שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹכֵל לָךְ״, ״שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם לָךְ״.
segments.en: § It is taught in the mishna with regard to «one who says to his fellow: I am avowed» from you, or another intimation of a vow, that the vow takes effect. «Shmuel said: In all» these cases, the vow does not take effect «until he says:» I am avowed from you with regard to «that» which «I eat» of «yours,» or: «That» which «I taste» of «yours.» Without this addition, the statement: I am avowed from you, is not considered even an intimation of a vow.
